rubric_items.reason: No new route, no request-driven lookup, only status copied from doctor, fixed-text UI, no logging. The single real weakness (non-null assertion at L60) is found. Scans attached and match impl.checks.json hashes.
SF-1 and every code claim point at the exact line (appointmentService.ts L57, L60, L68; AppointmentDetailPage.tsx L73), and each line matches the quoted text.
Minor fits SF-1. DOC-5 blocks deleting a doctor who has appointments (doctorService.ts L127-137, plus FK 23503), so the risk is defensive only. Reschedule uses the same pattern.
The fix direction is clear (replace the assertion with an explicit error). It does not say which error or status, and the global handler already returns a generic 500.
No false positives. SF-1 overstates impact a little by calling the failure 'unhandled' when the global errorHandler catches it.

findings.text: SF-1 calls the failure an 'unhandled error'. In fact the global errorHandler catches the TypeError, logs only the message and returns a generic 500. So nothing is disclosed, and the 'generic error' the fix asks for already exists.

cites.quote: would turn a broken invariant into an unhandled error
res.status(500).json({ error: { code: 'INTERNAL', message: 'Something went wrong' } });

findings.suggested_fix: Describe the impact as an opaque 500 (on action responses, after the mutation has committed), not as an unhandled error. Name the error to raise, e.g. an explicit HttpError with a generic message.
